title: Why New Orleans musicians resist leaving town
summary: Discussion of the New Orleans reluctance to go on the road, and Hug's own homebody nature.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: This seems to be something that's always struck me as sort of almost a tradition among New Orleans musicians, the reluctance to leave town. I guess Chicago, almost forced out because of the closing of Storyville, and then we know on the current pop charts, our hurt, you know, for a long time resisted leaving town, and so did Pete Fountain. Have you ever thought about this? Why is that there's such a reluctance on the part of major talents, such as yourself, to leave town? It seems like there are big markets elsewhere. There's lots of money. There's recognition and stardom that's not exactly attainable here. Have you ever given any thought as to why, generally,

Orleanians seem hesitant about going on the road? Well, I would imagine that it is the glamorous atmosphere that New Orleans offers, not money-wise, but certainly it has plenty of atmosphere, and if you're born here, you know what it is. It's just as you say, do you know what it means to miss New Orleans? Well, this is very true, and if you have ever been away for a while, why do you get this urge to come back? And, of course, I was always, as I said, sort of a guy that was stuck close to home, and, well, one time my uncle wanted me to go to New York, and my mother liked to have a fit because he was trying to talk me in the game, going to New York, and I think this sort of put a sort of damper on things, too.
